questions.prompt: In Angular, three components each need the same reference data, so the same HTTP call fires three times on page load. Cleanest fix?
options: Move it into a service and share one result — shareReplay, or a store.
Put the call in a base class the three components extend.
Fetch once in AppComponent and thread it down through @Input chains.
questions.explanation: This is what services are for. shareReplay(1) on the observable means one request, and every subscriber — now or later — gets the same value. Inheritance gives all three their own call, and prop-drilling from the root couples every component in between to data they don't use.

questions.prompt: This Angular component becomes slower every time the user navigates away and back. What is the red flag?
options: Observable names must not end with a dollar sign.
The component creates a subscription with no teardown; repeated mounts can leak the component and duplicate work. Use the async pipe or lifecycle-aware unsubscription.
questions.explanation: A long-lived observable can retain a destroyed component and keep delivering values. The async pipe, takeUntilDestroyed, or another lifecycle-bound strategy prevents duplicate subscriptions and memory leaks.
